coming.title: A sanity check of every working function in the viewer
coming.what: You opened the 9397 on 19 November: the steering did nothing under your hand, and with a motor running the page took seconds per frame. On 20 November you set the rule (257): a function too slow in the viewer to tell whether it works is not a working function. You then tried the 9397's steering after a first mend and found it still too slow, about 2 seconds for each small turn. Claude measured why: each small turn of a drag costs about 900 ms before the solver takes its first step, so one turn takes about 1,400 ms. The solver owner mends that first. The worker's sweep tries every working function in the viewer and writes a table of every function with its time for one step, which Claude puts on the Technic status page. All times so far, yours and Claude's, were taken while every core was busy with checks, so they are too high by a factor not known (261). The slowest functions are timed again on a quiet computer when the run is through, and you test on another machine. No function is held for speed until you have judged there where the line lies. The sweep also judges the working functions that a collision stops after a small turn (24 that should turn without end, 33 more stopped within 0.2 radian; example: the 42123 McLaren Senna's V8). Claude expects the 740 to fall by 50 to 120 in all. On 20 November the sweep's first pass went through all 740 working functions (267): the turn shows 566, does not show 144, and 30 wait for a look at the booklet. Of the 57 sets with every function working, 32 have every function shown. The 144 are not all real: in 28 the sweep did not free pins that the check frees, and in about 45 more it could not turn the control at all, which the pointer pass will try. Claude expects 30 to 70 real ones; the worker sorts them before anything is marked down. On the evening of 20 November the solver's working set was merged into preview and turned on (272): a drag that turns a part now works only on the pieces the drag moves. In the viewer on this machine the 9397's steering takes 15 ms for each step of a drag against 120 ms before, both measured one after the other under the same load; the first move of a drag still takes about 240 ms. The proof is a sample of 19 sets in which no function changed its result. In the night to 21 November three more things went in: big models open quickly again (274: the 42078 Mack Anthem in 5 s against 33 s, a fault Claude's own merge of 20 November had made), the first move of a drag no longer searches twice (275: the 9397's steering starts in 384 ms against 644 ms), and the day's full check of preview ran (278): the counts are the same, 740 work, and the check took 18% less time. The check found three functions in which the working set leaves one freely turning part out of place after the drag, with the result unchanged: the 42020 Twin-rotor Helicopter's rolling wheels (two thin beams, parts 125 and 126) and the 8274 Combine Harvester when pushed (a toothed half bush, part 1081). This was mended the same morning (285): the working set had thrown away a motion kept for the next step; with the mend all three come back whole. On 21 November the worker finished sorting the 144 (279). 100 are shown after all, once the sweep did what a user does: lift the model, press Shift, do the first steps, drag by pointer. On 21 November the check learned to mark a wheel, track or shaft that a collision stops by itself (311), which replaced 22 of the day's holds; 25 functions are still held at partly by hand, and the count of working functions is 698. Six of them are functions the booklet shows moving far and the viewer stops short (298). Of the others: in 29 a collision stops a wheel, track, fan or other part that should turn without end, or a bonnet or mast that the booklet shows moving far (the check stopped at the same place and still said works, which is the check's fault; 279, 288); in 12 the control turns or is pushed and the listed parts do not all move (279, 286); in 2 the drive seemed to slip in one long drag (286), which proved to be a fault of the sweep's own measure, so these two holds were wrong and are lifted, with a third of the same kind, the 42129's function 4 (293); and one is from 19 November. Two holds on the 8063 proved wrong and were lifted (282). About 8 more are doubtful and stay at works until tried properly. The sets with every checked function working are 52, were 57. The worker now sorts each of the 16 contacts into false or true and makes the check judge such a stop itself. Pull preview at the newest commit before you test on the quiet machines on 21 November.
